subject: Archaeology
title: Looting and the Antiquities Black Market
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Looting and the Antiquities Black Market.

hook.text: The illegal antiquities trade is worth billions. Looted objects pass through dealers, auction houses, and private collections.

buildup.text: Looters dig at night, ripping objects from the ground without recording anything.

discovery.text: ISIS funded its operations partly by taxing looting of ancient sites in Syria and Iraq — archaeology funded terrorism.

twist.text: Many looted objects end up in respected museums and private collections.

climax.text: The Met, the Getty, and the Louvre have all returned looted objects after investigations exposed stolen provenance.

punchline.text: Every looted artifact is a page torn from a book.

quiz.question: How did ISIS exploit archaeology in Syria and Iraq?
options: They sold museum admission tickets to fund operations
They taxed looting of ancient sites to generate revenue
They melted down bronze artifacts for weapons manufacturing
